ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s203.summary: Section 203 requires steering controls to avoid catching the driver’s clothing or jewellery. Passenger cars, three-wheeled vehicles and specified MPVs, buses and trucks up to 4,536 kg GVWR must also meet SAE J944 body-block impact testing at 24 km/h, with chest force limited to 11,120 N except for a cumulative 3 ms. Walk-in vans and vehicles meeting the specified TSD 208 requirements are exempt from those impact tests.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s203._why: summary: F015; own body 203(1)–(4): non-snagging controls; J944 impact at 24 km/h, 11,120 N and 3 ms; walk-in-van/TSD208 exceptions.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s208.title: MVSR s. 208 — Occupant Crash Protection and Seat Belt Installation
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s208.summary: Section 208 sets seat belt installation and fit requirements for enclosed motorcycles, passenger cars, three-wheeled vehicles, trucks, multi-purpose passenger vehicles and buses, with rules varying by seating position and vehicle type. It also requires specified vehicles and their manuals to conform to TSD 208 Occupant Crash Protection, with Canadian adaptations, exceptions and bilingual airbag warnings.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s208._why:
title: F016; own body 208(13): TSD208 Occupant Crash Protection; 208(1)–(6): seat-belt installation.
summary: F017; own body 208(1)–(6), (10)–(13), (15)–(25): vehicle/seat-dependent installation and fit, TSD208, adaptations and bilingual airbag warnings.
vehicle_categories: F190; own body 208(5)–(6), (13): explicit bus belt-installation and TSD208 requirements; retain other approved vehicle classes.
commodities: F191; own body 208(19), (25): airbag deactivation provisions and mandatory bilingual airbag warning labels support Airbags.

ca-mvsr-sor-2010-201.summary: SOR/2010-201 sets greenhouse-gas emission standards and fleet credit requirements for passenger automobiles and light trucks. The text held in this record also includes zero-emission-vehicle requirements beginning in model year 2026, incrementally leading to all new covered vehicles being zero-emission by model year 2035, with a separate system of compliance units. Current amendments should be checked at the official source.
ca-mvsr-sor-2010-201._why: summary: F018; own body SOR/2010-201 sections2(a)–(b),3(c)–(f): fleet credits and MY2026–2035 ZEV/compliance units; summary explicitly describes stored text, not verified current law.

ca-workbook-reg-0145-eccc-sor-2003-2._why: un_equivalent: F019; own body Related Regulations lists UNECE R83 alongside other instruments; no clause adopts it or accepts it as an equivalent/alternative. Clear unsupported mapping without asserting legal non-equivalence.

ca-workbook-reg-0359-motor-vehicle-tire-._why: un_equivalent: F021; own body Related Regulations lists UNECE R30 alongside FMVSS/CMVSS; no clause adopts it or accepts it as an equivalent/alternative. Clear unsupported mapping without asserting legal non-equivalence.

kr-kmvss-art56-2.summary: Article 56-2 defines EDR events as a cumulative speed change of at least 8 km/h within 0.15 s (including lateral change where recorded), irreversible safety-device deployment, or external pedestrian-protection-system deployment. It covers passenger cars except ultra-compact cars, vans up to 3.85 t GVW, and trucks up to 3.85 t except ultra-compact and towed vehicles; installation follows Table 5-25. The stored text includes amendments of 14 February 2025, effective 30 May 2025.
kr-kmvss-art56-2._why: summary: F079; own body Article56-2①1–3,②1–3,③ and amendment/effect notes: exact EDR triggers, distinct car/van/truck limits and Table5-25; root-modified value retained.

kr-kmvss-art94.summary: Article 94 sets forward and rearward field-of-view requirements for passenger cars and light-class vans; the forward-view table excludes ultra-compact cars. Windshields, windows to the left and right of the driver, and passenger-car rear glazing must have at least 70% visible light transmittance, excluding sun-shading areas outside the driver's field of view. All glazing in school vans for children must meet the 70% requirement.
kr-kmvss-art94._why: summary: F080; own body Article94①–③: forward-view ultra-compact exception, both left/right driver windows, passenger-car rear glazing, sun-shading exception and school-van glazing; root-modified value retained.

kr-workbook-reg-0597-noise-and-vibration._why: un_equivalent: F081; own body Related Regulations merely lists UNECE R51; no adoption, equivalence or accepted-alternative clause. Clear unsupported mapping without asserting legal non-equivalence.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s103.summary: Requires windshield defrosting and defogging systems, with three-wheeled vehicles covered when fitted with a windshield. Passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles must meet SAE J902 performance requirements and applicable J902 or J902a test procedures, with the modifications specified in this section.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s103._why: summary: F179; own body 103(2)–(4): general equipment requirement, windshield-dependent three-wheel scope and passenger/three-wheel J902/J902a performance/testing with modifications.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s104.summary: Requires windshield wipers with at least two speeds: one at least 45 cycles/minute, a lower speed at least 20, and at least 15 between the highest and a lower speed. Passenger cars and three-wheeled vehicles have minimum wiped-area requirements. Washer systems meet SAE J942 with specified modifications. Three-wheeled vehicle requirements apply when a windshield is fitted.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s104._why: summary: F180; own body 104(3)–(7): wiper frequencies, windshield-dependent three-wheel scope, minimum wiped areas and J942 washer modifications.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s105.summary: Subject to section 135 of this Schedule, multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses must conform to TSD 105, Hydraulic and Electric Brake Systems, with the indicator-lamp and warning-statement provisions specified in this section.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s105._why: summary: F181; own body 105(1)–(3): applicability is subject to section135, with indicator-lamp and warning-statement provisions.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s108._why: vehicle_categories: F182; own body 108(1): every truck is included without a GVWR cap; retain other approved categories and add Heavy truck.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s111.summary: Section 111 sets mirror construction, reflectance, mounting and field-of-view requirements for passenger cars, three-wheeled vehicles, motorcycles, MPVs, trucks and buses. School buses require specified outside mirror systems. It also requires rear visibility systems for specified vehicles up to 4,536 kg GVWR, subject to referenced FMVSS 111 manufacturing dates and Canadian exceptions.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s111._why: summary: F183; own body 111(1)–(6), (7), (11), (13), (16), (26)–(27): construction/reflectance, motorcycles, school-bus mirror systems and other light/heavy vehicle mirror rules. Root verified 111(29)–(33): rear visibility systems for specified vehicles up to 4,536 kg GVWR, referenced FMVSS 111 manufacturing dates, definition and Canadian exceptions.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s115.summary: Requires a 17-character VIN, unique within the specified 60-year manufacturing window. It must be indelibly marked on a permitted vehicle part or permanently affixed plate or label. Specified vehicle classes must have the VIN readable through the glazing without removing parts; snowmobiles have separate marking requirements.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s115._why:
summary: F184; own body 115(1)–(3): 60-year VIN uniqueness window, permitted indelible part/plate/label marking, selected-class glazing-readability rule and separate snowmobile marking.
vehicle_categories: F185; own body 115(1), (3) and TableI: all vehicles; TableI expressly lists Truck and Bus as well as retained classes.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s126.summary: Passenger cars, multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses with GVWR of 4,536 kg or less must meet TSD 126 for electronic stability control, or alternatively Annex 9 of UN Regulation No. 13H before the 01 series of amendments, subject to the Canadian adaptations in subsection (2).
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s126._why: summary: F186; own body 126(1)–(2): TSD126 or accepted Annex9 UNR13H before01-series alternative with Canadian adaptations; this patches summary only.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s201.summary: Section 201 applies to passenger cars and to multi-purpose passenger vehicles, trucks and buses with GVWR of 4,536 kg or less. It sets head-impact performance requirements for instrument panels and seatbacks, retention tests for interior compartment doors, and energy-absorption requirements for sun visors and armrests, with specified test procedures and exclusions.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s201._why:
summary: F187; own body 201(2)–(10): scope, instrument-panel/seatback head impact, interior compartment-door retention, sun visors and armrests with exclusions.
commodities: F188; own body 201(5), (8)–(10): interior compartment doors, energy-absorbing sun visors and armrests support Interior trim; retain the approved remaining commodities.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s206._why: vehicle_categories: F189; own body 206(1): truck scope has no weight cap; only Bus has the 4,536kg cap. Heavy truck is supported by the unqualified truck requirement.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s209._why: commodities: F192; own body 209(1)–(10): seat-belt assembly standard and adaptations; airbag is a condition for certain belt installation, not an airbag product requirement.

ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s215.summary: Section 215 of Canada's Motor Vehicle Safety Regulations requires passenger cars to have bumpers meeting either UN Regulation No. 42 paragraph 6 and the Annex 3 low-speed-impact test procedure, excluding Annex 3 paragraph 4 (version of 12 June 2007 with later 00-series amendments), or 49 CFR Part 581 (revised 1 October 2006). Conformity has been required since 1 September 2009.
ca-mvsr-c-r-c---c--1038-s215._why: summary: F193; own body 215(1)(a)–(b), (3): precise UNR42 Annex3 paragraph4 exclusion/version/amendments and Part581 edition; conformity date1Sep2009.

ca-mvsr-sor-2010-90._why: vehicle_categories: F194; own body SOR/2010-90 section101(3)(b)(v): CMVSS213.3 expressly covers custom disabled-person restraints designed only for school buses.

kr-kmvss-art104.summary: Article 104 sets side-door crush-resistance requirements for passenger cars excluding ultra-compact cars, and separate latch, hinge and retention requirements for hinged, sliding and ultra-compact vehicle doors. The latch and hinge rules include specified strength and inertia loads, with exclusions for certain vehicle and door types.
kr-kmvss-art104._why: summary: F320; own body Article104①–③: crush resistance plus separate door latch, hinge, strength/inertia and ultra-compact door requirements with exclusions.

kr-kmvss-art105.summary: Article 105 requires glazing performance prescribed by the Minister and sets passenger-car windshield retention and intrusion limits in a 48.3 km/h frontal barrier impact. Retention must be at least 50% per side with an automatic occupant protection device, or 75% of the full perimeter without one. Specified open-top, forward-control and light-class vehicles are exempt from the impact requirements.
kr-kmvss-art105._why: summary: F321; own body Article105①–③: glazing performance, 48.3km/h impact, 50%per-side/75%perimeter retention and listed exemptions.

kr-kmvss-art110.summary: Speedometers must be clearly readable in the driver’s direct field of view by day and night, cover the vehicle’s maximum speed, and use the specified scale graduations. At actual speeds of at least 25 km/h on flat roads, indicated speed must not be below actual speed and may exceed it by no more than one tenth of actual speed plus 6 km/h.
kr-kmvss-art110._why: summary: F322; own body Article110①–②: readability/range/graduations and 0≤V1−V2≤V2/10+6 at actual speeds≥25km/h.

kr-kmvss-art112-11._why: vehicle_categories: F323; own body Article112-11: wheels in passenger cars and towed vans/trucks/special-purpose vehicles≤3.5t; retain Passenger car/Trailer and remove powered Light truck.

kr-kmvss-art15._why: vehicle_categories: F324; own body Article15③1–4: explicit service, breakaway and parking-brake requirements for towed vehicles above0.75t support Trailer.

kr-kmvss-art15-2._why: systems: F325; own body Article15-2②2(c),②4: ESC startup self-diagnosis and fault lamp; no emission OBD requirements. Retain braking/ADAS/control tags.

kr-kmvss-art18._why: systems: F326; own body Article18 items1–3: insulation, wiring attachment and battery fastening/covering; no EMC emissions/immunity requirement.

kr-kmvss-art26.summary: Requires head restraints on front seats other than middle seats of passenger cars excluding ultra-compact cars, and of vans, trucks and special-purpose vehicles up to 4.5 tonnes gross vehicle weight. Item 3 excludes ultra-compact trucks and towed vehicles from its truck requirement; item 4 excludes ultra-compact special-purpose vehicles.
kr-kmvss-art26._why: summary: F327; own body Article26 items1–4: passenger cars separately from4.5t van/truck/special-purpose limits; root follow-up keeps item3/item4 exclusions under their own classes.

kr-kmvss-art27-2.summary: Passenger cars excluding ultra-compact and single-row vehicles require child restraint anchorages at two or more seats, including one in the second row. Each position has two lower anchorages and, except for convertibles, an upper anchorage, meeting the specified installation, marking and safety requirements.
kr-kmvss-art27-2._why: summary: F329; own body Article27-2 introductory scope and items1,7: two positions/second-row requirement, two lower anchorages and convertible upper-anchorage exception.

kr-kmvss-art34._why: vehicle_categories: F330; own body Article34①,④–⑤: towed-vehicle glazing expressly excluded and powered-window requirements are for passenger cars/vans; remove Trailer from this discovery filter.

kr-kmvss-art38.summary: Requires white main- and dipped-beam headlamps with specified installation and intensity standards, excluding towed vehicles. Ultra-compact vehicles up to 130 cm wide may use a single main- or dipped-beam lamp. Adaptive headlamps have separate requirements; primary dipped beams above 2,000 lumens require a washing device.
kr-kmvss-art38._why: summary: F331; own body Article38①1,②1,③,④: one-lamp exception for ultra-compact vehicles≤130cm, adaptive headlamps and>2,000lm dipped-beam washing.

kr-kmvss-art54.summary: Article 54 requires motor vehicles to have a speedometer meeting Article 110 and an odometer displaying total distance travelled. Subject to emergency-vehicle and maximum-speed exceptions, speed limiters are required for vans including school vans, trucks and special-purpose vehicles over 3.5 tonnes, high-pressure-gas tank trucks, and low-speed electric vehicles. Limiter settings are 110 km/h for vans, 90 km/h for the listed trucks/special-purpose vehicles and 60 km/h for low-speed electric vehicles.
kr-kmvss-art54._why: summary: F332; own body Article54①–③: speedometer/odometer plus mandatory speed-limiters, exact vehicle groups, exceptions and110/90/60km/h limits.

kr-kmvss-art97.summary: Article 97 sets seat strength and retention requirements, excluding side-facing seats, folding auxiliary seats and van passenger seats. Longitudinal forces apply at any adjustable position; the forward- or rearward-facing seat moment test applies with the seat at its rearmost position. Hinged and folding seats require locking and release devices, subject to stated vehicle/seat exceptions, and their locks must withstand the specified forces.
kr-kmvss-art97._why: summary: F333; own body Article97①–③: longitudinal loads at any adjustment, moment test rearmost, hinged/folding seat locks and specified exclusions.
